newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs off sharply on Wall St, options.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs off sharply on Wall St, options.

text.p: Brazilian shares dropped 3.01 percent in hefty trade by midafternoon, pressured downward by declines on Wall Street and sales of benchmark Telebras to cover options-related losses, brokers said.
"The market is very nervous, very volatile. We have options expiration today," said a dealer at local Crefisul brokerage.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 47 most-trade issues fell 341 points to 10,994 points on heavy volume of 1.508 billion reais ($1.39 billion).

Brokers said losses in New York combined with selling of blue-chip Telebras preferred to drive the market lower during a session marked by options expiration. "People were overbought in the spot market," one dealer said.
Telebras preferred dropped 2.99 percent to 132.90 reais and its common was off 4.47 percent at 117.509 reais.
But other major blue chips also were down, including federal power holding Eletrobras, which was down 3.30 percent at 527 reais.
The stock followed a general selloff among power stocks, as the Electrical Energy Index was down 3.39 percent at 3,233 points.

Brokers expressed concern the drop, the second consecutive session of heavy losses in Sao Paulo, would prompt local stock funds to begin pre-emptively selling Brazilian shares to cover possible heavy withdrawals.
A similar trading pattern, sparked by currency devaluation fears, provoked a sharp drop in local shares in mid-July.
